primary_task: Build a PowerShell 7 automation script that performs Azure infrastructure tasks (for example Azure VM lifecycle across subscriptions) with validated subscription/tenant context.

requirements.name: pwsh (PowerShell 7+)
requirements.evidence: CI/CD pipelines requiring PowerShell 7+ with modern .NET interop; Uses PowerShell 7 language features where beneficial

requirements.name: Az PowerShell module / Azure CLI
requirements.evidence: Azure automation using Az PowerShell + Azure CLI; Az module version compatibility checked
requirements.basis: Not stated. Az modules come from the PowerShell Gallery (not in egress_allow); azure-cli is on PyPI ("pip from PyPI" is open). Would need to check the PowerShell Gallery host.

requirements.name: azure
requirements.evidence: Subscription/tenant context validated; Auth model chosen (Managed Identity, Service Principal, Graph); "Automate Azure VM lifecycle tasks across multiple subscriptions"
requirements.basis: lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, ...)"

requirements.name: *.azure.com / graph.microsoft.com
requirements.evidence: Azure infrastructure orchestration; Graph API automation for M365/Entra

requirements.name: Azure Key Vault
requirements.evidence: Secure handling of secrets (Key Vault, SecretManagement)
requirements.basis: lacks: "connectors or integrations other than the tools listed"

requirements.name: GitHub Actions
requirements.evidence: "Create GitHub Actions automation for infrastructure builds"
requirements.basis: description: "The user's GitHub account is usable through the github connector and through the gh CLI via the proxy."

notes: I took the description's lead case (Azure infrastructure orchestration) as representative: running and validating it needs pwsh (listed as unavailable), Azure credentials (lacking) and Azure endpoints (denied). Under the reading that the deliverable is only script text written to a file without running it, the agent can author it and the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE but untested. A GitHub Actions-only request would also be ACHIEVABLE on the authoring side. Note that pwsh for Linux is published as a GitHub release, but the manifest explicitly lists pwsh in unavailable_programs, which I followed literally. Unknown: Az module source (PowerShell Gallery).
